course_description:
This is a restricted entry course. To be eligible to apply to POLS3801 students must (a) be enrolled in a program in which POLS3801 can be credited, (b) completed at least 12 units of POLS courses, and (c) achieved a GPA of 5 or higher for these courses. Eligible applicants are not automatically guaranteed a place in the course. The Internship is based on a mutually agreed partnership between the student and an external organisation. Interns are expected to carry out a project on a topic/issue of direct interest to the external organisation. Previous internship partners have included: Queensland Parliament MPs, Queensland Government Departments, local government councillors, federal MPs and Senator's Electoral Offices, Asia-Pacific Centre for the Responsibility to Protect (UQ) and the Centre for Policy Futures (UQ), community or not-for-profit organisations, and other national and international, governmental and non-government agencies. All additional costs incurred by students undertaking this course remain the responsibility of the student. Please note: Students accepted to participate in the PEATLI project in either the summer or winter break may be eligible to apply for enrolment in POLS3801 for the following semester. Students participating in the UQ Embassy Internship Program in Summer semester may also be eligible to enrol in POLS3801 in Semester 1 or Semester 2. From 2026, Bachelor of International Studies students may apply for POLS3801 if they also meet the standard eligibility criteria noted above. Further information including how to apply is available here .

An internship within the School of Political Science and International Studies is an elective 2-unit course. To be considered for the POLS3801 internship, students need to be enrolled in a relevant undergraduate degree at the University of Queensland and have completed 2 years of full-time equivalent study.ﾠ

The internship is designed to provide students with the opportunity to utilise the research and report writing skills developed throughout their undergraduate program in a relevant work context. A wide variety of organisations may offer internships, in the public, private, and community sectors.

Students who enrol in an internship are expected to produce a high quality research report based on their agreed research topic. Students are placed in the most appropriate available organisation to ensure they will be able to further their research skills and expand on their knowledge.

Students are placed with a variety of organisations, depending on availabilityﾠand locational convenience. In previous years these opportunities have included placements in the offices of elected representatives in the three levels of government (Local, State and Federal). In second semester only, there is also a special program managed throughﾠthe Queensland Parliament to work with Parliamentary support staff and with the office of a state MP. There are usually several opportunities to work with research institutes, private sector consultancies, and a variety of community and advocacy organisations. Very occasionally there may be opportunities in public service departments and statutory authorities.ﾠ

The School endeavours to ensure that placements are available in all research areas relevant to the majors taught within the School and for social science and humanities students more broadly.ﾠ

There is a limited formal teaching program for this course. Students enrolled in an Internship will be primarily engaged in the preparation of a research report for their Internship organisation and are likely to spend up to one day per week with their designated organisation. The research report is supervised jointly by the student's mentor in the Internship organisation and by an academic staff member of the School of Political Science and International Studies. The classes scheduled for this course will be primarily concerned with organisational issues related to the course,ﾠguidance in report writing requirements and skills, and providing support for interns in their placements.
In addition, students undertaking the QPRI (Queensland Parliament) placement will have specific tasks set by the Parliamentary staff. Where different from the standard assessment tasks for POLS3801, the QPRI requirements will prevail.
course_aims: POLS3801 aims to establish Internship placements that provide students with the opportunity to utilise the analytical, research and communication skills developed throughout their undergraduate program in a relevant work context.ﾠIn particular, the course seeks to:

learning_outcomes.description: Clearly define the scope and limitations of a policy research topic in conjunction with leaders in a partner organisation.
Design, develop and implement an in-depth analysis of an identified workplace issue or problem.
Co-develop policy improvements where relevant in conjunction with supervisors.
Produce a comprehensive and professional report addressing the issue or problem.
Engage in a professional, ethical and productive manner with team colleagues in the partner organisation.
Demonstrate professional behaviour appropriate to an early career professional.
Identify and articulate skills and knowledge developed through workplace professional experience.

Assignments for this course will be submitted electronically via Blackboard and using Turnitin .
In uploading an assignment via Turnitin you are certifying that it is your original work, that it has not been copied in whole or part from another person or source except where this is properly acknowledged, and that it has not in whole or part been previously submitted for assessment in any other course at this or any other university.
When you successfully submit your assessment to Turnitin after previewing the uploaded document (to make sure that you have chosen the correct file), you should see the “Submission Complete!” message. After this, a downloadable Digital Receipt will display on your Assignment Dashboard. It is your responsibility to download the Digital Receipt as proof of submission. Turnitin will not send this receipt to you automatically.
If you don’t see the downloadable receipt on your assignment dashboard, you should regard your submission as unsuccessful.
If the submission was not successful:
Note the error message (preferably take a screenshot). Go to your assignment page and see if it is possible to submit again. If you cannot submit again, then email your course coordinator immediately.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
Unless an extension is granted, penalties for late submission apply. Students are penalised 10% of the maximum possible mark allocated for the assessment item for every calendar day that an assessment item is late.
Marks will be deducted each day for up to 7 calendar days, at which point the submitted item will not receive any marks unless an extension has been approved. Each 24-hour block is triggered from the time the submission is due.

assessment_details.title: Presentation (and discussion)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The powerpoint slide deck must be provided to the POLSIS WIL Manager prior to the presentation for uploading: polsiswil@uq.edu.au This is NOT submitted through Turnitin. Students will be invited to select a time on Monday 12 October, with some carry-over times on Tuesday 13 October 2026. Interns are expected to present a 5-7 minute overview of their internship research/report. They will then defend and elaborate on their presentation in response to questions from fellow students and the course coordinator. Questions and discussion will take 7-10 minutes. Interns are expected to prepare and use a PowerPoint (about 6 slides), and to address the following five points; 1 - The aim(s) of the research 2 - The central research question 3 - The method(s) being deployed 4 - The main findings (2 slides) 5 - Ensuing implications and/or policy recommendations This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Research Report (4000 words)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Work integrated learning. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Interns are to write a 4000 word internship report. The report should clearly articulate (1) the broad topic being investigated, (2) a specific central question, (3) the method used to examine this question, (4) the main research findings, and (5) the implications of these findings for current policy practice and/or stakeholder engagement. A good report will typically discuss each of these five aspects in this particular order, so you may want to consider structuring your research report in this way. For those students participating in the Queensland Parliament Research stream, the requirements of the Queensland Parliament program prevail over the arrangements suggested for other Internship students. The completed report must be submitted (a) to the School of Political Science and International Studies using Turnitin (for marking purposes), and (b) to the internship organisation, in either electronic OR hardcopy format, depending on the internship organisation's preference. learning_activities.topic: Seminar 1 INDUCTION SEMINAR - 28 July 2026. Learning outcomes: L01

Getting to know the organization - Familiarize yourself with the organization's overall aim(s) - Gain a solid understanding of the aim(s) of your project - Ensure you are in agreement with your supervisor Learning outcomes: L01, L04, L05, L06, L07

Reaching agreement about the research project - Articulate the research question your research will examine - Consider potential research methods (in addition to Literature Reviewing) - Ensure you are in agreement with your supervisor - Apply for Ethical Clearance if research involves human participants Learning outcomes: L01, L04
Seminar 2 RESEARCH SCOPING SEMINAR - 18 August 2026. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05, L06, L07

Reviewing relevant social science literature - Review the existing literature examining your research topic - Identify relevant existing knowledge and possible knowledge gaps - Decide whether literature reviewing will suffice to meet organization's needs Learning outcomes: L05

Independent Research - Review the existing literature examining your research topic - Identify relevant existing knowledge and possible knowledge gaps - Decide whether literature reviewing will suffice to meet organization's needs Learning outcomes: L02, L04, L05

Independent research Finalise 'Literature Review' section for the final research report - Deploy additional research method (if necessary) - Data collection (statistics, policy documents, archives, survey/interviews*) * NOTE: Ethical Clearance required if research involves human participants Learning outcomes: L02, L06, L07
Seminar 3 RESEARCH & RESEARCH REPORTING SEMINAR - 15 September 2026. Learning outcomes: L02, L04, L05
Independent research Learning outcomes: L02, L04, L05

Independent research - Data collection (statistics, policy documents, archives, survey/interviews) -- Write and/or revise draft research report, incorporate feedback Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05

Seminar 4 12-13 October 2026. Oral Presentations on research project (7 minute overview with powerpoint slides, plus questions and discussion) Students will attend both a morning and afternoon session of presentations. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06, L07
Independent research and Report writing revisions of draft report, consult with supervisors and agree on presentation and referencing style Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Independent research and Report Submission - Write/revise final research report - Submit Final (4000 word) Research Report (see Section 6. Assessment) Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
